about: Sourced numbers behind Plot Twist. August footprint = the extension service's recommended in-row spacing (spacing is set so neighbours just touch at maturity).

crops.name: indeterminate tomato
crops.sun: full sun (UMD: at least 6 h/day, prefers 8-10 h)

sources.quote: Allow two to three feet in all directions between vining plants.
18”-36” in rows x 48”-60” between rows.
They grow to three to five feet long, sometimes more.
65 - 90 from transplant.
Full sun requires direct light at least 6 hours/day; prefers 8 - 10 hours/day.
Plant seeds one-fourth inch deep in flats ... Start tomatoes from seeds indoors, five to six weeks before planting outside.
single plants 2’- 3’ in-row x 3’- 5’ between rows; Hills (two to three plants per hill) 3’- 4’ in-row x 4’- 6’ between rows.
Sow seeds 4 to 6 inches apart in the row, then thin to 12 to 15 inches apart. Transplants go about 15 inches apart.
Height: 1 ft. 0 in. - 3 ft. 0 in.; Width: 2 ft. 0 in. - 25 ft. 0 in.
Days to maturity: 50 - 65 from transplant.
about 55 days after planting
Full sun.
Plant the seeds 1/2 inch deep; can be planted from seed or transplants.
Sow seed directly into the garden after the danger of frost has passed and soil has warmed.

crops.name: sweet basil
crops.sun: full sun (6+ h); Clemson: grows reasonably well in part sun (6 h)

sources.quote: With a spacing of 2 feet between plants and 3 feet between rows
Space plants at least 2 feet apart.
annual herb that matures about 18 inches tall
Height: 0 ft. 4 in. - 3 ft. 0 in.; Width: 0 ft. 4 in. - 1 ft. 2 in.
Plant basil in a full sun location, where it receives 6 or more hours of direct sun daily in summer.
Although basil prefers full sun, it grows reasonably well in part-sun (six hours of sun per day).
Plant basil seeds 1/4-inch deep; start seeds indoors four to six weeks before outdoor planting.
can also be directly seeded in the garden after the threat of spring frost has passed

crops.name: leaf lettuce
crops.sun: tolerates partial shade (4-6 h direct light/day); full sun fine in spring/fall

sources.quote: Leaf, cos, or butterhead, 4"- 10" in-row x 12"- 24" between rows
plants 6 to 10 inches apart in the row
Days to maturity: 40 - 80, depending on the type.
about 75 days after planting (leaf lettuce)
Tolerates partial shade (4-6 hours of direct light/day) but grows well with full sun in spring and fall.

Increasing day-length and high summer temperatures usually cause seedstalk formation (bolting) and bitter flavor. ... use tall crops and trellises to protect the late spring lettuce plantings from direct afternoon sun. Shade cloth can help to protect summer-grown lettuce from direct sunlight and high temperatures.
harvested when plants are 5 to 6 inches tall
seed one-quarter inch deep; leaf lettuce is direct-seeded
